results.summary: This design implements an ASCON AEAD cryptographic processor with a shared permutation core and a UART command interface. It supports ASCON-AEAD-128 encryption and decryption, and includes an on-die ring-oscillator entropy source with NIST SP 800-90B health tests and an ASCON Hash_DRBG for key and nonce generation. The design also integrates a debug pin for raw entropy characterization. It is notable for its reconfigurable implementation of the ASCON family standardized in NIST SP 800-232.

This design is a multi-protocol communication controller that supports UART, SPI, and I2C transmission modes from a single module. It is controlled via the Tiny Tapeout input and bidirectional pins. The design is compact and integrates all three protocols in one module. It is notable for its versatility in supporting multiple serial communication standards.

This design is a waveform generator that produces various waveforms using a lookup table and NCO techniques. It includes a CORDIC algorithm for phase-to-amplitude conversion. The waveform selection and configuration are controlled through the Tiny Tapeout input and bidirectional pins. It is notable for its DSP-oriented signal generation capabilities.

This design is a digital tremolo modulation controller intended for guitar pedal applications, generating a PWM signal that can be filtered into an analog control voltage. It uses a counter and comparator to produce the PWM waveform. The modulation rate is controlled by the input pins. It is notable for its simple implementation of a classic audio effect.

This design demonstrates a simple hardware-based data masking technique that can be used in secure communication systems. It uses an LFSR to generate a pseudo-random mask that is XORed with the data. The design is intended for educational purposes to illustrate basic side-channel countermeasures. It is notable for its simplicity and potential application in security.

This design consists of a password checker, a lock controller, and a top module. It can be tested with a provided testbench using iverilog. The design implements a simple security mechanism for controlling access. It is notable for its educational value in demonstrating sequential logic and state machines.

This design performs fast modular addition and subtraction arithmetic arrays using specialized combinational subtraction matrix logic blocks without slow division operations. It is optimized for speed by avoiding division. The design is suitable for applications requiring efficient modular arithmetic. It is notable for its innovative approach to modular computation.

This design provides an on-die entropy source using a ring oscillator with NIST SP 800-90B health tests. The entropy is conditioned through ASCON-Hash256 and fed into an ASCON Hash_DRBG for key and nonce generation. A debug pin exposes raw ring-oscillator bits for post-silicon entropy characterization. It is notable for its integration of a TRNG with cryptographic conditioning.

This design implements the ASCON-Hash256 and ASCON-XOF128 hash functions. It uses the ASCON-p permutation core for all modes. The design is intended for cryptographic hashing applications. It is notable for its compliance with NIST standards.

This design provides the ASCON-p permutation core used in ASCON cryptographic algorithms. It supports both p[12] and p[8] variants. The core is shared across multiple modes. It is notable for its efficiency and reusability.
